title: [Chapitre] VII. Analysis situs (troisième mouture) : notes manuscrites (23-26/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from p.74): M is a set of 'pieces' (e.g. segments or sub-strings of a topological 'ficelle', i.e. a string) carrying a symmetric disjointness relation X ∥ Y. P is a set of points, with a support map |·|: M → 𝔓(P). The conditions are (i) X ∥ Y ⇔ |X|∩|Y| = ∅, and (ii) a T0-type separation of points by supports. For A ⊂ M, cosupp A = A^∥ = {X : X ∥ Y for all Y ∈ A} and supp A = cosupp cosupp A = A^∥∥. supp is the closure operator of the Galois connection given by ∥, and Σ_M, the set of 'supports' (closed sets A = supp A), is a complete ortholattice. The underlying question, raised on p.74, is whether such data determine P up to unique isomorphism, for instance via a canonical identification of Σ_M with (part of) 𝔓(P).

On this page Grothendieck extends the support map to subsets, |A| = ⋃_{X∈A}|X|. He then asks whether (*) supp A ⊂ supp B ⇔ |A| ⊂ |B| holds; supp A ⊂ supp B is equivalent to A ⊂ supp B by general closure-operator nonsense. Using cosupp-reversal and condition (i), he rewrites X ∈ cosupp A as |X|∩|A| = ∅. So supp A ⊂ supp B becomes (•): for every X ∈ M, |X|∩|B| = ∅ ⇒ |X|∩|A| = ∅. This is clearly implied by |A| ⊂ |B|, giving ⇐. For ⇒ one would need a piece X meeting |A| but missing |B| whenever |A| ⊄ |B|. He says this is unclear and he knows no counterexample offhand. He then specialises to B a support (B = supp B), where the left side reads A ⊂ B and gives |A| ⊂ |B| trivially.

On p.76 this becomes a Lemma: under (i), |A| ⊂ |B| ⇒ supp A ⊂ supp B, with equivalence when B is a support. The Corollary is that A ↦ |A| embeds Σ_M order-injectively into 𝔓(P). He then studies how meets and joins of supports behave under |·|. The purpose is a Stone/point-reconstruction type representation of the abstract 'lattice of supports' of a space by subsets of its points: point-free analysis situs.
errors: Gap, not an error: the general implication supp A ⊂ supp B ⇒ |A| ⊂ |B|, which Grothendieck left open, is false, and trivially so. Take P = {1,2,3} and M = {X = {1,2}, Y = {2,3}, Z = {2}}, with ∥ meaning disjointness. Condition (i) holds, and the separation condition (ii) also holds (Z separates 2 from 1 and from 3; X separates 1 from 3). No two pieces are disjoint, so cosupp of any nonempty set is ∅ and supp of it is M. Then A = {X}, B = {Y} gives supp A = supp B = M but |A| ⊄ |B|. So the restriction to B a support in the next step is genuinely necessary.

Minor: the step 'supp A ⊂ supp B ⇔ A ⊂ supp B' is fine. More precisely, the converse holds whenever |supp B| = |B|, a slightly weaker hypothesis than B = supp B; this is not stated, but it is harmless.

ideas.what: Abstract disjointness relation ∥ on a set of pieces; supp = biorthogonal closure, cosupp = orthogonal; Σ_M = closed sets
ideas.modern_name: Orthogonality space / Galois connection, biorthogonal closure, complete ortholattice of closed subsets

ideas.what: Extending the point-support |·| to sets of pieces and showing it embeds the lattice of supports into 𝔓(P) (Lemma and Corollary on p.75–76)
ideas.modern_name: Representation of a region/contact algebra or ortholattice by subsets of points; mereotopology point-reconstruction
ideas.usually_credited_to: Stone (1936–37), Whitehead/de Laguna/Tarski (point-free geometry), Düntsch–Vakarelov (region-based topology)

ideas.what: Question whether disjointness data on pieces determine the point set P up to unique isomorphism
ideas.modern_name: Point-free (pointless) topology / reconstruction of points from regions; 'tame topology' foundations
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme §5 announces a programme of 'topologie modérée' but not this formalism

missed.claim: Grothendieck's 1986 'Analysis situs' notes set up topology axiomatically from a disjointness (orthogonality) relation on pieces and their biorthogonal 'supports'. This is essentially the framework of orthogonality spaces and mereotopological contact algebras, which the literature on tame topology / Esquisse §5 does not connect to his programme.
missed.quote: X ∈ cosupp A ⟺(def) X ∥ A ⟺(def) ∀Y∈A, X∥Y ⟺ ∀Y∈A, |X|∩|Y|=∅ ⟺ |X|∩|A|=∅
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It is of historical interest for how Grothendieck intended to found 'topologie modérée' point-free. The mathematics itself is elementary and known in the orthogonality-space / region-based-topology literature.

deep.surprise_reason: The page contains an elementary closure-operator lemma in a Galois-connection setting. Its interest is purely as documentation of the unpublished point-free foundations of Grothendieck's 'analysis situs' programme. The open question he raises has an easy counterexample.
transcription_corrections: The label over the third equivalence, transcribed '(iii)[?]', probably refers to condition (i) of p.74 (written with an M subscript, cf. 'condition (i)_M' on p.76), not a condition (iii).
Margin note: likely 'NB |∅| = ∅, et si [la condition (ii)?] ... , |M| = P', i.e. noting that the union of all supports is P.
'(ou encore A ⊂ supp B)' is a parenthetical reformulation of the left side of (*), not of the right side.
